1 Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner June 2025 NEWNEWS FRS FROM THE BOOM THE BOARDARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners ADA COUNTY PARAMEDICS CHIEF ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT AFTER NEARLY THREE DECADES OF SERVICE After nearly 30 years of service at Ada County Paramedics, Chief Paramedic Shawn Rayne has announced his intent to retire on October 31, 2025. “I grew up in Ada County and knew that I wanted to spend my life and raise a family here, giving back to the place I call home,” Rayne said. “I consider myself lucky to be able to work 29 years with some amazing healthcare providers in a cutting-edge EMS system.” “Our deepest gratitude for Shawn’s outstanding service to Ada County,” said the Ada County Board of Commissioners. “Shawn has been a steady, consistent, and reliable leader for Ada County Paramedics during a time of significant change. His leadership skills and his well-informed advocacy, compassion and support for his EMS team have distinguished Shawn’s service. We will miss Shawn’s knowledge and calming presence, but we are happy knowing he will be out enjoying hunting, fishing, and horse riding soon.” Rayne began working at Ada County Paramedics on December 1, 1995, as a paramedic after serving in the United States Army for four years. He was promoted several times throughout his EMS career, serving as an Education Captain, Field Training Officer, Field Captain, and a Battalion Chief. Rayne was promoted to Deputy Chief in 2005. He briefly left ACP in 2019 when he was tasked to be the EMS Division Chief at the Boise Fire Department for 17 months. Rayne returned to take the role of Chief Paramedic in 2020, helping guide Ada County Paramedics through the COVID-19 pandemic. Some highlights of Rayne’s career include being a Tactical Medical Team member, a Special Operations Team member, and a member of the Ada County Paramedics Honor Guard. Rayne has also served as Chair of the Ada County Cities Emergency Services System (ACCESS) administrative committee, President of the EMS Division of the Idaho Fire Chiefs Association,

2 a member of the Idaho EMS Sustainability Task Force, and a member of the Idaho EMS Advisory Committee. “I can’t help but feel proud of the accomplishments we have made and strides we have been able to take. The thing I am most proud of, however, is knowing that we have over 140 of the best EMS providers you can find in this country. Our leadership, education and training, logistics, and equipment are all second to none. I feel confident that this department will continue to thrive as I ride off into the retirement sunset.” We will miss you very much Shawn. # Page 3^page=3
3 FIREWORKS BANNED IN PARTS OF UNINCORPORATED ADA COUNTY Interactive map shows exact areas where fireworks are banned If you live in Idaho, you know wildfires are a significant threat to lives, homes, and property every year. According to the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC), this year’s wildfire threat in our area will likely be severe. “Ada County has a higher potential for large fires due to abundant grasses from the last two wet winters, coupled with a forecasted warmer and drier than normal summer,” said Jim Wallmann, Meteorologist, National Interagency Coordination Center Predictive Services. Ada County Commissioners voted Tuesday, June 17, 2025, to prohibit fireworks in parts of Unincorporated Ada County that constitute a severe fire threat. Chairman Rod Beck and Commissioner Tom Dayley voted in favor of the ban, with Commissioner Ryan Davidson voting against the ban. This map shows the areas of Unincorporated Ada County where fireworks are prohibited. 2025 FIREWORKS BAN AREAS “A significantly increased fire danger affects all of the Western United States right now,” said Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley. “We’ve seen the catastrophic results in nearby states, and we are doing what we can here in Ada County to minimize the danger to lives and property.” Where is Unincorporated Ada County? Unincorporated Ada County is roughly 847 square miles of the county that are not within the city limits of Boise, Meridian, Kuna, Garden City, Eagle or Star. Unincorporated Ada County is home to more than 63,000 people. Ada County’s total acreage is 542,512. Please contact the city in which you live to learn of any city-specific fireworks prohibitions in place. Ada County Commissioners have voted to prohibit fireworks in unincorporated Ada County for more than twenty years.

4 2025 FLOAT THE BOISE RIVER News crews gather at Ada County’s Barber Park for Announcement Friday, June 20, 2025, was the start of the 2025 Float the Boise River season. This year, the start date coincided with the first day of summer in the northern hemisphere. There are many things you and your friends and family can do to make the experience enjoyable. Check out Ada County Parks & Waterways to learn more. Thank you to the community for making this annual rite of passage a beloved and special tradition for everyone. Thank you to our partners at Boise Parks and Recreation and Boise Fire Department for collaborating on all the planning involved in announcing a safe start date. If you’re new to the experience, remember - the Boise River is wild, so always be prepared, and float at your own risk. Here’s something else to remember – typically the Boise River is around 50 degrees Fahrenheit. Brrrr It’s the Law Safety is always first. Idaho Law requires anyone under 14 to wear a life jacket/vest

5 Ada County’s FY26 Budget Presentations and Deliberations wrapped up in mid-June. The final Ada County FY26 Budget will be adopted in August 2025. Counties in Idaho begin their fiscal year in October. This year’s presentations focused on mandates required by the Idaho Legislature. Each department head and elected Ada County Office holder outlined programs and services they are required to perform under state law. You can read County Mandates Under Idaho Law here: SERVICES AND PROGRAMS MANDATED BY THE IDAHO LEGISLATURE ADA COUNTY COMPLETES FY26 BUDGET DELIBERATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS Ada County is proud to provide live streaming of our budget presentations each year. You can find every presentation given to the board on YouTube. WATCH ADA COUNTY FY26 BUDGET PRESENTATIONS “Each year during our budget process, we scrutinize every dollar being spent in Ada County,” said Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck. “We rely on our dedicated department heads and fellow elected officials to provide details on each service, program, and initiative that serves our communities.” We encourage you to watch these hearings and learn exactly what counties provide to you, your family, and the greater community.”

# Page 6^page=6
6 Congratulations to Bob Batista on 25 years of service as Director of Expo Idaho and the Western Idaho Fair. Bob’s roots in the fair industry began in Great Falls, Montana, and his leadership experience spans the Montana State Fair, MetraPark in Billings, and Solano County Fair in California. Since joining Ada County in 2000, Bob has transformed Expo Idaho into a thriving, self-funded destination hosting over one million visitors annually. Expo hosts more than 175 diverse events spanning everything from large-scale trade shows and multi- day festivals to cultural celebrations, Quinceaneras, and community meetings. Under Bob’s leadership, revenue has grown by nearly 300%, and significant improvements—like a new Main Gate and Administration Building—have enhanced the 240- acre campus. Bob has also shaped the Western Idaho Fair into the state’s largest event, drawing over 250,000 attendees each August. A passionate advocate for entertainment and the fair industry has been instrumental in its success. He has held several leadership positions in national and regional associations, earning a Hall of Fame induction from the Rocky Mountain Fair Association in 2016. His vision helped guide the repurposing of the grounds post-horse racing, leading to two major developments: The Park at Expo Idaho, a 50-acre public park that will include nature trails, open green BOB BATISTA CELEBRATES 25 YEARS WITH ADA COUNTY spaces and recreation areas; and Boise Pro Soccer which will anchor a new stadium and professional training complex – both slated to open in 2026. These projects represent a transformative next chapter for Expo Idaho and Ada County. Bob’s dedication and collaborative spirit have left a lasting legacy. Over 25 years, Bob has partnered with dozens of County Commissioners, Advisory Board members, and community stakeholders. Through every transition and challenge, he has remained a tireless advocate for Expo Idaho and the role it plays in enriching our community. Please join us in honoring his remarkable 25 years of service to Ada County and Expo Idaho. Pictured L-R: Hans Bruijn, Becki Woodbury, Kasie Morrison, Lonna Breshears, Expo Idaho Director Bob Batista, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, Administrative Specialist Kelly Sarich, and Ada County CommissionerTom Dayley.

7 SHELLY HARRIS 25 YEARS AT ADA COUNTY Shelly Harris began her career in Ada County on June 8, 2000. Shelly started as a legal assistant in the Magistrate Division, which was then located in the basement at Barrister. She not only developed her skills during that assignment, but also helped develop new attorneys, some of whom are supervisors in the office today. Shelly moved to the Felony Division in 2003 and was promoted to a Support Staff Supervisor in 2011. Shelly found her passion in our screening unit. Her knowledge and experience in that unit are of paramount importance. She works efficiently with our law enforcement partners and makes sure that arrests and requests for warrants are processed in a timely manner for the proper administration of justice. Shelly takes immense pride in her work and the assistance her team provides to our office. Congratulations, Shelly, on 25 years! Learn More about Career Opportunities and Ada County’s Benefits Package https://adacounty.id.gov/human-resources/

# Page 8^page=8
8 The Ada County Assessor Office is setting the pace for others to follow. Assessor Rebecca Arnold and staff were honored to host special guests from Tokyo on Thursday, June 13, 2025. The group is traveling the United States and stopped in Boise to learn how Ada County uses oblique photography to assist with appraisals. If you’re unfamiliar, oblique photos are taken from small planes at an angle – a valuable visualization tool for our appraisers. The visitors from Tokyo work in the Fixed Assets, Property Tax Division, and Bureau of Taxation for the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. Tokyo has a population of nearly 15 million people. Ada County was honored to host our special visitors and is thankful our practices in Ada County are being recognized as far away as Tokyo. After our visitors left Boise they were heading for stops in Seattle, Washington, and Austin, Texas. TOKYO GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS VISIT ADA COUNTY ASSESSOR’S OFFICE ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/

9 BIG CHANGES AT ADA COUNTY’S EXPO IDAHO The County is six months into a 24-month project One of the most significant and dramatic transformations ever of an Ada County property is happening now. You can’t really see all the construction from the corner of Chinden Blvd. and Glenwood St., where Expo Idaho is …. But tucked behind that Ada County property where you attend the Western Idaho Fair each year, construction is underway on a 50-acre world-class park. Check out these progress photos! But wait, there’s more. Owners of Boise’s new professional soccer team Athletic Club Boise are building a soccer pitch at Expo Idaho. (We didn’t learn until recently that soccer fields are actually called pitches.) Part of that deal with the county means both the Turf Club and Grandstands will be totally modernized and retrofitted. Thank you to photographer Michael McCullough for the excellent images and drone footage we use in our monthly progress videos. Have you watched those yet? Check out Ada County’s YouTube
